FR-028.title: The replaced launch behaviour is not reintroduced, and a build fails if it is.

FR-001.title: The launch ends at exactly one of: the main screens, sign-in, machine setup, or a stated stop.

FR-002.title: The launch names each piece of work before performing it.

FR-003.title: Every wait on the launch path has a stated maximum and none is unbounded.

FR-004.title: A stopped launch states a cause specific to what stopped it.

FR-005.title: An error is shown in a strip at the bottom of the launch window without covering the list of work.

FR-006.title: A machine with no configuration does not reach the main screens by any route.

FR-007.title: Machine setup is authorised only by IT Department or Developer, and that authorisation does not open the main screens.

FR-008.title: Every route out of machine setup that is not completion ends the application with a stated reason.

FR-009.title: A machine whose configuration is removed, revoked or unreadable is treated as unconfigured at the next check.

FR-010.title: Session validity is judged by the store clock, not the computer clock.

FR-011.title: A session is cleared when the person signs out, before the application restarts.

FR-012.title: An account holding a temporary credential is refused after five failed attempts, including with the correct value, and the refusal survives a restart.

FR-013.title: The set-a-new-password step opens only after the temporary credential has been accepted.

FR-014.title: A remembered sign-in is held against the person in the store and encrypted, and an unreadable key falls back to the ordinary sign-in form.

FR-015.title: A computer whose hardware identity cannot be read is admitted.

FR-016.title: A stopped launch offers to repeat the failed work.

FR-017.title: Resetting is offered only where resetting could remove the cause.

FR-018.title: Resetting states what it will reset before acting and affects only this machine configuration, never people, roles or permissions.

FR-019.title: A fault that can be repaired without the person involvement is repaired without asking.

FR-020.title: Repeating failed work repeats only that work and what follows it.

FR-021.title: Every diagnostic is written to the store with severity, area, machine, person, error kind and message.

FR-022.title: Identity and machine facts are available to the rest of the application for reading only, and only the launch may change them.

FR-023.title: A person preferences are held against the person in the store.

FR-024.title: The list of locations to hide belongs to the whole plant and is changeable only by IT Department or Developer.

FR-025.title: Only what is needed to reach the store is kept on a computer, apart from the local copy of pictures.

FR-026.title: The copy of pictures is best effort and cannot stop the launch.

FR-027.title: Whether the external system can be reached is settled before the main screens open.

FR-029.title: How long a session lasts is changeable from the settings panel, and only by IT Department or Developer.

FR-030.title: Every setting that is restricted to particular roles today keeps the same restriction.

FR-031.title: The cases found by the three read-only sweeps are recorded in the repository as the acceptance surface, and every case is either covered by a test or recorded as no longer applying, with its reason.

decisions.decision: Rebuild MTM_Waitlist.Startup in place under the same project name: the solution entry and the two project references are re-pointed rather than re-invented, and the composition-root split is preserved. Rejected a new project name, which adds edits and widens the window where the tree does not build.

Delete the old startup surface first and prove removal with a placeholder window before building anything new, so a green build at that point means the removal is complete rather than that new code compensates for it. Rejected building the new pipeline alongside the old and switching over at the end.

Defer StartupDebugLog to Phase 6 and StartupState to Phase 4 instead of deleting them with the rest of the surface: 489 call sites and roughly twenty consumers mean deleting either in Phase 2 leaves the tree uncompilable and the Phase 2 gate unreachable.

The replacement logging seam is unconditional, with no Conditional attribute, because StartupDebugLog is Conditional DEBUG and therefore records nothing at all in a Release build, which is exactly what SC-003 requires to change.

Gate the ignored-locations write with a new key permission.settings.ignored_locations_edit rather than narrowing the existing key. FR-024 needs two roles to change it while FR-030 needs every existing restriction to hold, and the existing key is granted to seven roles, so narrowing it would remove read access from five. Rejected narrowing the existing key, and rejected gating the write in the UI only.

Add three new permission keys and do not reuse permission.settings.computers for machine setup. No key today contains machine, log or session; machine setup has a different blast radius from the Settings computers screen because it admits a computer to the fleet before anyone signs in. Rejected reusing permission.settings.computers, whose baseline is already exactly IT Department and Developer at 1 and every other role at 0.

Store the remembered sign-in in a new table auth_remembered_sign_ins keyed by person and machine. FR-014 needs it decrypted and held in the store, and it cannot live on user_active_sessions because sign-out clears that while surviving sign-out is its whole purpose. Rejected columns on core_users_profiles, columns on user_active_sessions, and a local DPAPI file.

Resolve the shared key file at its UNC path and treat it as read-only. X: is a per-user mapped drive that does not exist for another account, session or service, and the file pre-exists and is likely shared with other MTM authentication. Rejected generating a new key and rejected storing the key in appsettings.json.

The seven scoped preferences move into the existing config_settings_values store with no new storage, because the scoped store and its rank function already exist and PictureEnlargePreference already uses them, so each migration is one substitution. Rejected a new user_preferences table, which would duplicate scope precedence that already exists.

Repurpose ops_startup_logs as the one log store rather than renaming a successor: the identifier is pinned verbatim by the spec, the table already carries correlation and chain-hash columns, and it has no writer today. Rejected a new ops_application_logs table, which renames a pinned identifier for no gain.
A blank sign-in name now ends the identity in PersonIdentityService.ResolveAsync
decisions.why: a resolve that finds nobody must not leave the previous person signed in; the store-holds-nobody path already ends it, so the two answers now agree
decisions.rejected: leaving the early return as it was, which kept the previous identity standing

decisions.decision: Completed T187 before T020
decisions.why: Three of the nine procedures T020 deletes still had live callers, so the deletions were unsafe until the capability moved
decisions.rejected: Deleting the procedures first, which would have broken the Settings computer screen and the machine-facts read at runtime

decisions.decision: MachineFactsService reads the registry by name through sp_core_computers_registry_lookup_by_name_get and accepts the row only when its stored address matches this machine
decisions.why: The procedure it used is retired by T020, and confirming the address keeps the name-and-address identity the old read enforced
decisions.rejected: Keeping the retired procedure, which contradicts the approved deletion set

decisions.decision: Session length is seeded as sessions.length_hours at all_users scope, defaulting to 8 hours
decisions.why: Research D17 fixes the default and the scope but no artifact named the value key, so this task had to
decisions.rejected: Storing hours inside the permission key, which is a boolean gate and not a value

decisions.decision: The locations-to-hide plant row is stored with value_type text in normalized, uppercase, comma-separated form
decisions.why: It must round-trip the shape IgnoredLocationsService already returns, and text is the vocabulary this table uses for a readable value
decisions.rejected: Introducing a json value type, which no consumer parses

decisions.decision: UserManagementLiveIntegrationTests session fixtures moved onto user_active_sessions
decisions.why: The rebuilt session service does not exist yet, so the store seam is the furthest the case can move while still proving the rule
decisions.rejected: Retiring the case, which would have dropped a proven FR-011 guarantee

decisions.decision: The launch pipeline owns the two routing reads rather than reading a step's prose diagnosis
decisions.why: a step reports what it did and the contract gives it no routing member, so the verdict has to be read from the service that owns it
decisions.rejected: a shared holder the readiness step writes its verdict to, which would be a second source of the same fact

decisions.decision: The routing read after read-machine-configuration runs under that step's own stated maximum
decisions.why: a wait the person cannot see is still a wait, and FR-003 bounds every wait on the launch path
decisions.rejected: an unbounded read outside the runner

decisions.decision: A second entry while a launch runs joins the run in progress instead of starting one
decisions.why: the contract says a re-entrant entry returns without starting anything, and the caller still needs an answer
decisions.rejected: returning Blocked, which would show a stop for a launch that never started

decisions.decision: A catalogued step with no implementation is passed over and stays in the count
decisions.why: the later phases of this same feature supply each implementation, and a placeholder that reported success would put a line on the feed for work that never happened
decisions.rejected: a pending-step placeholder type, which is scaffolding for a phase that lands in the same feature

decisions.decision: ILaunchPipeline.End carries the abort route to the host
decisions.why: the surfaces own the UI that states the reason and the host owns the exit, and ProcessEnding is the only event that carries it
decisions.rejected: calling the process-lifecycle seam from each surface, which would leave ProcessEnding raised by nobody

decisions.decision: A name that names a path is not denied by the fragment it also carries
decisions.why: logging-contract section 6 grants the shared key file's path as the one secret-adjacent value that is written, and the blunt fragment match dropped it for containing the word key
decisions.rejected: narrowing the deny-list itself, which would let key material through

decisions.decision: the gate asks for sp_auth_user_credential_get and fails closed when it cannot be read
decisions.why: no surviving procedure returns credential material, and a gate that cannot check authority must not authorise anybody
decisions.rejected: an interface with no implementation, or reading the hash through sp_auth_user_row_get, which deliberately omits credential columns

decisions.decision: the gate authorises on permission.settings.machine_configuration rather than on two role codes in code
decisions.why: the key is what the declaration says this gate reads, and its baseline is the two roles that hold it
decisions.rejected: a hard-coded role check beside the seeded baseline

decisions.decision: the setup screen saves through IMachineConfigurationService itself
decisions.why: a display name another computer holds has to be refused on the screen and asked for again, which is the spec edge case
decisions.rejected: holding a draft for the pipeline save step, which reports a refused name as a stopped launch

decisions.decision: every terminal outcome now reaches the host through the hand-back event
decisions.why: the setup surface could not appear at all while the event fired for the main screens only
decisions.rejected: changing the host launch entry point instead, which is another phase's seam

decisions.decision: the abort statements, the route set and the screen derived state are internal
decisions.why: the naming rules allow one public type per file and this phase grants no new model file
decisions.rejected: new public model and interface files outside the phase file list

decisions.decision: One attempt costs one credential check: the sign-in surface makes the check and the check-credential step reports the recorded answer, making it only when none was recorded (the remembered path)
decisions.why: a second check in the step would spend a second attempt against the temporary-credential limit for one typing
decisions.rejected: checking again in the step, and letting a refusal surface as a blocked launch instead of staying on the form

decisions.decision: The session digest is computed salted once at issue and held in memory, and that same digest is presented when the session is validated
decisions.why: the validation read returns no salt, so a second computation would have to guess the material the first used
decisions.rejected: computing the digest over the token alone, which would have left the stored salt decorative

decisions.decision: The machine gate reuses MachineFactsService.RefreshAsync for the registry read
decisions.why: one read means the gate and the readiness steps cannot hold two opinions about whether this computer is registered
decisions.rejected: a second registry read written for the gate

decisions.decision: Sign-out ends the store session first, then clears the identity, then restarts; a store that cannot clear the session refuses instead of restarting
decisions.why: restarting over a session that still stands would show the person a signed-in application they asked to leave
decisions.rejected: restarting anyway and reporting the store fault afterwards

decisions.decision: LaunchSessionService, SignOutService, SignOutOutcome, IProcessRestarter and AppProcessRestarter are public
decisions.why: the public ShellViewModel exposes SignOutAsync and takes the service in its constructor, so the types could not stay internal
decisions.rejected: making ShellViewModel internal

decisions.decision: The remember-me choice is reversible: an explicit sign-in with the box clear forgets what this machine remembered for the person, while the remembered path leaves the stored choice alone
decisions.why: on a shared shop-floor computer a choice made once must not outlive the person changing their mind, and someone arriving through the remembered path never saw the box so nothing they did should change it
decisions.rejected: letting an unchecked box leave the earlier payload in place, which would leave a person remembered after asking not to be

decisions.decision: The remembered-sign-in payload is sealed with an authenticated cipher (AES-GCM: 12-byte nonce in the vector column, 16-byte tag carried behind the ciphertext in the payload column) rather than AES-CBC with PKCS7 padding
decisions.why: Microsoft Learn states that unauthenticated CBC decryption with verifiable padding is exposed to padding-oracle attacks, and this fall-back is observable by whoever presented the row, so a difference between a padding failure and a tamper failure is exactly the signal an oracle needs
decisions.rejected: AES-CBC, which is what the design first used; and CBC with a separate keyed MAC, which needs somewhere to keep the MAC and the table has one payload column and one vector column

decisions.decision: The stopped launch reads its cause from the feed's last non-best-effort StepFailed line rather than from a new pipeline property
decisions.why: The pipeline hands the host an outcome and not a diagnosis, and this phase may not restructure that seam; the feed is the read-only record the surface already draws
decisions.rejected: Adding a blocked-state carrier to ILaunchPipeline, which would restructure the seam and put a second account of the stop beside the feed

decisions.decision: BlockedStateCause is classified from the step that failed: a Machine-category step is this computer's own configuration, everything else is the store
decisions.why: The data model has one row for a broken or unreadable configuration and one for an unreachable store, and store-reachability fails before any Machine step, so a Machine-step failure means the store did answer
decisions.rejected: Matching on the diagnosis prose, which is written for a person to read and is free to change

decisions.decision: The parts repaired without asking are this machine's scope-supplied rows only (MachineConfigurationParts.ScopedPreference), never the display name, the description or the picture sources
decisions.why: FR-019 forbids a quiet repair that loses something the person chose, and those three are exactly their decisions
decisions.rejected: Repairing the whole configuration quietly, which would discard the name and description they typed

decisions.decision: A quiet repair is attempted once per process, and a fault that came back after one is asked about
decisions.why: A fault that survived its own repair would otherwise be repaired again on every stop, and the launch would loop without ever saying anything
decisions.rejected: Retrying the quiet repair on every stop

decisions.decision: BlockedStateViewModel is registered transient, and the host rebuilds the surface for each stop
decisions.why: The view model is a reading of the lines written so far, so a second stop needs a second reading
decisions.rejected: A singleton reading the feed once, which would show the previous stop's cause behind a question about this one

decisions.decision: StartupRecoveryService was removed from the retired-symbol guard's pattern set and from its removed-type inventory
decisions.why: T123 and the plan's project tree rebuild StartupRecoveryService in place under the same name, exactly as US1 did for SplashWindow, SplashPage and SplashViewModel; the contract IStartupRecoveryService stays forbidden
decisions.rejected: Renaming the rebuilt type, which would contradict T120's file path and the plan's tree

decisions.decision: the copy's ceiling is 1048576 characters, recorded in contracts/logging-contract.md section 7.1
decisions.why: the point past which a clipboard payload stops being pasteable text and starts being a file transfer, and high enough that a page of ordinary entries is never cut
decisions.rejected: a smaller messaging-sized ceiling, which would cut a normal page and be hit routinely

decisions.decision: LogPanelEntry is a read shape beside StoreLogRecord
decisions.why: the write shape carries what a write needs; the read shape carries the row identity, the store clock and the two chain columns the write procedure computes for itself
decisions.rejected: one type serving both, which would make the chain and the timestamp nullable for the writer and re-promised for the reader

decisions.decision: the clipboard is a delegate on the view model whose default calls Clipboard.SetContentWithOptions with both options false
decisions.why: the refusal path has to be exercisable without a live clipboard, and the options overload answers false where Clipboard.SetContent throws
decisions.rejected: calling Clipboard directly from the command, which cannot be tested and would raise a fault while reporting one

decisions.decision: the Settings module now references MTM_Waitlist.Logging
decisions.why: the panel reads the log read shape and formats its copy through the logging module, and Logging references Core alone so the new edge adds no cycle
decisions.rejected: moving the formatter into the Settings module, which T183 pins to MTM_Waitlist.Logging

decisions.decision: the group toggle changes what the next read asks for rather than reading on the spot
decisions.why: a control that read the instant it was ticked would be a read the reader did not ask for, and it left the panel holding one answer while the screen claimed another
decisions.rejected: auto-loading on the toggle, which also raced the reader's own press

decisions.decision: the copy's labels are stable English rather than localised
decisions.why: the copy is diagnostic evidence pasted to somebody who does not have the store, so a translated label would change what the evidence says
decisions.rejected: localising the formatter's labels, which would also make the logging module read a resource file it has no business reading

decisions.decision: Declared the scoped-preference seam as a Core contract implemented in Settings, so the Core services, the Setup dialog and the Waitlist store can all take it without a module reference they must not have.
decisions.why: MTM_Waitlist.Core references nothing and Setup does not reference Settings, while the configuration read that reaches config_settings_values lives in Settings. This is the same shape as IRequestItemAllottedMinutesStore, which exists for the same reason.
decisions.rejected: Calling the two stored procedures directly from each of the six consumers, which would have repeated the scope and value-type logic six times.

decisions.decision: Prefers the plant-wide override over this machine own configured folder, then the machine folder, then the shipped default.
decisions.why: A plant-wide decision applies to every computer, so it is the site answer, and the machine row is what machine setup captured for this machine. Keeping that order leaves the disagreement line the storage panel shows with a subject.
decisions.rejected: Machine configuration winning outright, which would have made SharedFolderResolution.MachineDisagrees unreachable and left the panel disagreement line dead.

decisions.decision: Enforces the ignored-locations edit entitlement inside the service write rather than only in the view model command.
decisions.why: FR-024 and FR-029 require the restriction where the action happens; a hidden control is not a permission, and the service is the seam every writer passes through.
decisions.rejected: Gating only in SettingsViewModel, which leaves the write reachable by any caller that does not draw the screen.

decisions.decision: Moved the single declaration of the session-length key into MTM_Waitlist.Core and had the launch and the settings panel both reference it.
decisions.why: The launch module and the Settings module do not reference each other, so one shared declaration is the only way the two cannot drift.
decisions.rejected: A second copy of the key string in the settings panel, or a Settings reference to the startup module.

decisions.decision: Recorded T188 in the file rather than re-pointing the session case at the session service.
decisions.why: The case asserts that an unrelated account update leaves a session row alone, which is a store property. The session service can only judge a session this process issued, and the retired repository and its six procedures are gone.
decisions.rejected: Driving the case through a faked session service, which would have proved what the fake does rather than what the store does.

decisions.decision: Replaced ten local-settings test doubles with one shared in-memory store double that records reads and writes.
decisions.why: Five had to be replaced and five were already dead; one shared double keeps the scope handling in one place and lets a test assert that a refused change wrote nothing at all.
decisions.rejected: Five near-identical per-file doubles.

decisions.decision: The session-length seed and the validator name auth.session_length_minutes, not sessions.length_hours
decisions.why: the launch resolves that key at plant scope and the settings panel writes it, so the seeded row under the other name was dead and the validator was checking a key nothing read
decisions.rejected: changing the launch to read sessions.length_hours, which would leave the panel writing a second key

decisions.decision: The two hardware-identity cases state the machine they are about instead of borrowing the host's
decisions.why: the step reads the machine from its context, so the branch is reachable by construction and the case stops standing down on a workstation that presents an address
decisions.rejected: recording the case as retired, which would have dropped a real branch

decisions.decision: S13 keeps the sweeps' group summary and adds a walkable catalogue beside it
decisions.why: the sweeps' original 111-item breakdown was never committed, so enumerating it would mean inventing it; the twenty-three cases the specification records are listed with a disposition each
decisions.rejected: reconstructing 111 items from the group counts

decisions.decision: The rebuilt launch is one living capability, startup-launch, replacing the two whose code is gone
decisions.why: the old split existed because the file-based log path was a concern of its own, and that path is deleted
decisions.rejected: keeping the startup row and adding a second, which would leave a capability matching no code

decisions.decision: The stalled-share acceptance case names a stored credential as the wrong way to reach it, and was left unrun.
decisions.why: Reaching the picture step needs a person actually signed in, and every account on the store carries a temporary-credential marker whose value was shown once and never stored. Writing a credential in would make the run evidence about a fixture this work invented rather than about the application.
decisions.rejected: Writing a password hash into core_users_profiles, signing in, running the case, then rolling the credential back.

decisions.decision: The seed issues the documented placeholder 0000, properly salted and hashed, rather than the 4330 in use on this machine.
decisions.why: The code and tests already name 0000 as the legacy temporary credential that must be accepted, so the value's meaning is unchanged and only the broken encoding is repaired. Committing 4330 would put a credential the owner actually uses into source control for no functional gain.
decisions.rejected: Writing 4330 into the seed so a fresh install matches this machine exactly.

decisions.decision: The seed issues 4330, and the schema validator applies seed files only when given -ApplySeeds.
decisions.why: The owner asked for the seed to ship the credential in use. Separately, the validator applied every seed file whenever a schema validated, and seed_dev_masked_baseline truncates and rewrites core_users_profiles, auth_roles_catalog, auth_roles_assignments, config_settings_values and core_computers_registry. Because the CI workflow points the script at a real store through secrets, a pull request touching any Database/**/*.sql file silently replaced that store's accounts and permission baselines. A validating check must not be a writer.
decisions.rejected: Leaving seed application on by default and documenting the hazard, which had already destroyed a hand-set credential during this session.

decisions.decision: Whether a step is a long wait is derived from the step's own declared target rather than from a list of waiting steps.
decisions.why: A step that names what it is about is reaching for something this computer does not hold - the store, the share, the external system - and those are the waits with no proportion to report. Writing the waiting steps out as a list would be a second account of the catalogue that could drift from it, and the two examples named in the request (the picture cache and a store connection) both fall out of the rule.

decisions.decision: The launch window's frame is removed through the overlapped presenter, and the surface carries its own Close button.
decisions.why: A title bar cannot hide itself - the caption buttons stay system-controlled for as long as one is drawn, and AppWindowTitleBar in Windows App SDK 2.0 has no member that removes it. SetBorderAndTitleBar(false, false) is the one call that does it, and both parts have to be false, because a window that keeps its border keeps a caption with it. No frame means no drag area, so the surface needs its own way out.

decisions.decision: The folder dialog is a seam the application implements, and the setup screen only asks for it.
decisions.why: A folder dialog has to be owned by a window, and an unpackaged desktop process has no ambient window to parent it to, so the implementation has to know which surface is on screen. Putting that in the view model would have made the screen undrivable by a test, so IFolderBrowserService sits in Core, its one implementation sits in the application where the windows are, and App.CurrentSurfaceWindow answers which window owns a dialog.

decisions.decision: The setup form is pre-filled from the store first and the shipped defaults second.
decisions.why: A machine whose configuration is being corrected should start from what it currently has. The compiled defaults only fill what is missing, so the screen never overwrites a value that exists, and the dunnage folder - which has no shipped default - is left empty with a hint rather than given an invented path.

decisions.decision: The machine-setup screen captures only the computer's name and an optional note. The three folder fields, their Choose-folder buttons and the picture-source half of the save are removed.
decisions.why: The shared pictures and keys folders are the same for every computer, so a screen that sets them per machine writes the organisation's answer once per PC and lets two machines disagree. They already belong to the org-wide settings the storage-paths panel writes.

decisions.decision: The per-computer picture sources are retired: the rows in config_images_locations, the write procedure behind them, and the launch step that writes them all go.
decisions.why: With the folders org-wide there is no second writer and no per-machine override to keep current. Keeping the rows readable would leave two accounts of the same fact.

decisions.decision: When the configured share cannot be reached, a picture path resolves under the local cache root and the launch states that the copies on this computer are being used.
decisions.why: The cache already exists for part pictures. Resolving to it keeps a workstation working through a share outage, and saying so on the launch surface keeps the fallback from being invisible - a picture that is quietly a day old is a fault report waiting to happen.

decisions.decision: The keys the application reads are copied into the local cache folder at startup, refreshed when the share holds a newer copy, and scoped to only the keys actually read - which is one today.
decisions.why: Two answers were given about how many keys to copy. They agree on the current code, which reads exactly one key, so the rule is 'the keys the application actually reads, and no more'. The tighter scoping wins if a second key is ever added.

decisions.decision: A locally cached key is acceptable, under three conditions: only under the local cache root, only for the keys the application reads, and with the copy and its path recorded in the log. It is never written back to the share.
decisions.why: This amends the startup module's FR-025, which says nothing is kept on the machine except what it needs to reach the store and the local copy of the pictures. A cached key is key material on disk, so the amendment has to be written down rather than assumed.

decisions.decision: The shared pictures folder and the shared keys folder belong to the plant, not to a computer: they are held once in the settings the storage-paths panel already writes, and the machine-setup screen captures only the computer's name and an optional note. A computer counts as configured once the store holds its name. When a share cannot be reached a picture resolves under the local cache folder and the launch states that the copies held on this computer are the ones being used; a picture with neither a copy nor a reachable share is reported missing, never drawn from a stand-in. The keys the launch reads are cached under the local cache folder, refreshed when the shared copy is newer, never written back, with the copy and its path logged. FR-025 is amended to name that cached key as a second exception, held to three conditions: only the keys the launch actually reads, only under the local cache folder, never written back.

Reconcile note on the two key answers. 'Every key the application reads' and 'only the one key file' pull against each other. They agree on the code as it stands, which reads exactly one key (SharedKeyFileSource in MTM_Waitlist.Startup/Services/RememberedSignInService.cs). The rule was taken as 'the keys the application actually reads, and no more', with the tighter scoping winning if a second key is ever added. This is recorded as the reading, not as something the owner confirmed.

The 63 recorded concerns were worked through on 2026-09-28. Thirty-six were already resolved, superseded or accepted and were removed. The remaining 27 were put to the owner as questions and every one is answered; the answers are in spec.md under Clarifications and the work is Phase 12 in tasks.md (T205-T229). Three answers changed requirements rather than confirming them: remember-me is withdrawn in favour of a previous-users list on the sign-in screen (FR-014); the launch window states the work under way on a single line with no history, reversing the earlier one-line-per-operation rule (FR-039); and the launch window must open centred while the administrator sign-in and the machine setup screen are reworked with cards, padding and margins (FR-045, FR-046).
The two installer defects are to be applied to the store by running the installer, which the owner authorised; the corrected scripts are already committed, so the store is the only thing outstanding.
The hardware-identity case that cannot be exercised on this workstation is accepted as environment-gated rather than unproven-by-oversight.

A store that must appear unreachable cannot be aimed at a black-hole address: the application substitutes this machine's own store when the configured host does not answer, so case A uses a port closed on both hosts and case B uses a listener that accepts and then says nothing.

The acceptance watcher stops on the first window that is not the launch window, not on a quiet period: the splash deliberately sits still while a store is being contacted, so stillness is what a healthy still-working launch looks like.

Every account in the local store carried the retired 0000 placeholder with a NULL salt, so nothing could verify a sign-in at all. The seed says so itself ('the credential is the placeholder the accounts above use, so none of these can log in'), and the gate's own test uses 0000 as the credential that must be refused. A fresh install therefore has no way in until a credential is issued out of band.
